Here’s a polished, kind version coming from Eric, keeping it collaborative and clear:

---

Hi [Name],  

Thank you for taking the time to lay everything out. We really appreciate the flexibility and the thought behind the options you shared.  

After reviewing internally, I think we are aligned that moving toward a more content-focused approach makes the most sense for this next phase. On our end, The Luxora Collective will take over the day-to-day posting, captioning, and engagement across our social channels so we can keep everything consistent with our broader strategy.  

One direction that feels like it could work well for both sides would be to treat this as a short runway. We would be open to continuing through the end of May, shifting into a content-only role focused on shooting and editing starting now, and then wrapping things up cleanly at that point.  

If we go this route, we would want to be a bit more intentional about how production is structured so we can maximize the value of the remaining time. From our side, that would include more deliberate planning around which med spas we are shooting at and how that content is being used, along with a more defined creative approach so the content feels elevated and purposeful. We would also want consistency in video length and format so it aligns with how we are distributing it across platforms.  

In terms of cadence, increasing shoot frequency would be important. Ideally we would aim for three shoot days per month, understanding we may land somewhere in the two to three range depending on scheduling.  

Turnaround time will also be key for us. Since we will be handling execution internally, we would need edited content delivered within about one week of each shoot so we can keep everything moving efficiently.  

We are happy to work through the details together, but wanted to share this direction to make sure we are aligned on expectations and that this feels productive for both sides over the next couple of months.  

Looking forward to hearing your thoughts.

Here’s a sharper, more direct version that clearly sets the boundary while still keeping it professional:

---

Hi [Name],  

I appreciate you laying out these options and being flexible here. I do want to make sure we’re fully aligned moving forward.  

The original intent behind bringing you on was for full social media management, not just content capture. If the direction is shifting away from management and toward purely video production, then the structure of the engagement would need to reflect that change in a meaningful way.  

If we are now taking on the responsibility of monitoring and managing all of our own social channels internally, we would need significantly more value on the production side to justify continuing. That would look like increased onsite shoot time, more frequent shoots across 3 to 4 medspas per month, a higher volume of edited content, and a noticeable lift in overall editing quality and creative direction.  

In that case, it would also make sense to fully remove social media management from the scope and reposition this as a true content production partnership.  

We’re open to finding a structure that works, but it needs to feel like a step up in execution and output, not a reduction in support.  

Let me know your thoughts and we can align on next steps.

Here’s a tightened version with that point added in clearly:

Hi [Name],  

I appreciate you laying out these options and being flexible here. I do want to clarify something important on our end so we can stay aligned.  

The original intent behind bringing you on was for full social media management, not just content capture. Shifting to a model where management is removed and we’re only receiving raw assets doesn’t fully support what we actually need, especially at this stage of our growth.  

Especially if we now have to monitor and manage all of our own social channels internally, the value of the engagement needs to reflect that shift.  

If we’re going to remain in the contract, we’d want to restructure the engagement to better align with that. Ideally, that would look like 4 hours onsite per shoot, across 3 to 4 medspas per month, with a stronger emphasis on higher-quality production and noticeably improved editing. The content needs to feel elevated, intentional, and aligned with the level of brand we’re building.  

We’re absolutely open to making this work, but it would need to be a true improvement in both execution and output, not a reduction in scope.  

Let me know your thoughts on adjusting the structure this way, and we can move forward from there.
